name: Real Geeks
description: Real Geeks is a real-estate website, lead-generation and Lead Manager CRM platform that routes leads from websites and advertising sources into agent follow-up workflows and third-party destinations.
agentUseSummary: Real Geeks is visible as a provider-access and privacy-review preview. Relay will not collect shared partner credentials, ingest lead data or receive outgoing lead webhooks until Real Geeks approves a scoped, auditable production integration.

capabilities.label: Review a bounded Real Geeks lead integration
capabilities.description: If provider approval is obtained, expose only exact-site, privacy-reviewed and typed lead events under immutable grants and explicit action policy.

blocked.label: Capture Real Geeks partner credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask an operator to paste the product-level Basic Auth username and password that Real Geeks reuses across every granted client site.

blocked.label: Grant sites or expose lead identity
blocked.description: Running site authorization, collecting site UUIDs, or reading lead names, emails, phone numbers, property searches and activity histories is unavailable.

blocked.label: Create or update leads and activities
blocked.description: Creating leads, updating lead records, assigning users or adding property-view, message and other activities is unavailable.

blocked.label: Receive Real Geeks lead webhooks
blocked.description: Relay will not register a destination, accept signed lead or activity pushes, or store destination secrets before provider and privacy review.

blocked.label: Run Real Geeks actions before review
blocked.description: No Real Geeks tool is callable until the provider supplies scoped credentials, automated tenant grants, rotation and revocation, webhook replay controls, limits and production distribution terms.

approvalProfiles.label: Real Geeks partner and lead-data review
approvalProfiles.description: Connection, installation and agent actions remain unavailable while integration depends on shared product credentials and sensitive multi-site lead flows.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tools are callable under Real Geeks' current shared partner-credential and lead-routing contract.
No Hermes tools are callable under Real Geeks' current shared partner-credential and lead-routing contract.

providerSetup.blocker: The Incoming Leads API requires provider registration and issues one Basic Auth username/password per product, reused across every Real Geeks client site that grants access. Site grants and UUID delivery are partly manual. Incoming endpoints create or update sensitive lead records and activities; Outgoing destinations push lead and activity data to a registered URL with a shared signing secret. Public materials do not document granular scopes, independent per-site credentials, automated revocation, credential rotation, webhook replay requirements or production distribution terms.
providerSetup.nextAction: Request a production partner contract from Real Geeks with scoped per-site credentials or delegated OAuth, automated grant and revocation, immutable site claims, credential rotation, signed webhook timestamps and replay protection, rate limits, deletion handling, audit identifiers, privacy terms and a staging tenant. Then implement only typed, purpose-limited lead events with explicit approvals and retention controls.

evidence.supports: Real Geeks documents a partner API for sending leads into Lead Manager and receiving real-time lead and property-search activities from client sites.
The Incoming API uses one registered product's Basic Auth credentials across granted client sites, identifies each tenant by site UUID, and permits lead creation, updates and activity writes.
Outgoing destinations receive new leads and activities at a configured URL using a shared signing secret and partner identifier.
Real Geeks positions its APIs as advanced custom integrations for moving sensitive lead and contact data in or out of the CRM and warns that incorrect sends can overwrite or duplicate leads.
API credentials require a provider access request rather than self-service user authorization.
